title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask a friend if they're free, suggest what to do, agree where and when to meet, say you're on your way or stuck in traffic, and cancel without upsetting anyone.
intro:
This is the Marathi you'll use every week: texting the group about the weekend, fixing a time at the usual **कट्टा** or **टपरी**, and the classic message **मी निघालोय** 'I've left' (which, everyone knows, sometimes means 'I'm about to leave').

The grammar is the grammar of plans: **'let's'** with **-ऊया** (जाऊया, भेटूया) and **'shall we?'** with **-आयचं का?** (जायचं का?), the bare commands friends use with each other softened with **ना**, **रे** and **की**, and how to say you're **about to** leave, **on the way** or **almost there**.

grammar.title: Let's… and shall we…?: -ऊया and -आयचं का?
grammar.body:
**Let's: stem + ऊया.** Take the verb stem (करणे → कर) and add **-ऊया**: **करूया** 'let's do', **भेटूया** 'let's meet', **बसूया** 'let's sit'. Stems ending in a vowel add **-ऊया** too: जा → **जाऊया**, खा → **खाऊया**, घे → **घेऊया**, ये → **येऊया**. It is often introduced with **चल** (to one friend) or **चला** (to a group): **चल, जाऊया** 'come on, let's go'.

The shorter **-ऊ** (करू, जाऊ, भेटू) means the same 'let's' and also 'we'll': **उद्या भेटू** 'see you tomorrow'.

**Shall we?** Either add का: **जाऊया का?** 'shall we go?', or use the very common **-आयचं का?** (lit. 'is it to be done?'): **जायचं का?** 'shall we go?', **कुठे भेटायचं?** 'where shall we meet?', **काय करायचं?** 'what shall we do?'. -आयचं needs no subject, which is why it's the natural way to ask the group.

The trap: **आपण जाणार आहोत** is a statement ('we're going to go'), not a suggestion. To propose, use **जाऊया** or **जायचं का?**

examples.en: Come on, let's eat out today.
Shall we go to a film on Saturday?
What time shall we leave tomorrow?

grammar.title: Telling friends what to do: ये, ये ना, ये की
grammar.body:
With a friend you call **तू**, a command is just the bare stem: **ये** 'come', **जा** 'go', **थांब** 'wait', **सांग** 'tell', **बस** 'sit', **निघ** 'leave', **चल** 'come on'. To a group, or to anyone you call तुम्ही, add **-आ**: **या, जा, थांबा, सांगा, बसा, निघा, चला** (unit 11).

A bare command can sound abrupt, so friends add a little word at the end:
**ना** — a soft 'please / do': **ये ना** 'do come', **सांग ना** 'go on, tell me'.
**रे** (to a man) / **गं** (to a woman) — friendly: **लवकर ये रे**, **थांब गं**.
**की** — impatient 'come on!': **चल की!** 'come on, let's go!', **सांग की!** 'just tell me!'

The 2nd-person **future** with ना is an even softer request: **येशील ना?** 'you'll come, won't you?'

**Don't:** तू → stem + **-ऊ नकोस** (उशीर करू नकोस 'don't be late'); तुम्ही → **-ऊ नका**.

The trap: **ना** after a command is a softener, not 'no'. 'Don't' is **नकोस / नका**.

examples.en: Wait, I'm coming too. (to a woman, woman speaking)
Everyone come to the katta at seven.

grammar.title: About to leave, on the way, almost there
grammar.body:
**I've set off:** the past + आहे, contracted: निघालो आहे → **निघालोय** (man), निघाले आहे → **निघालेय** (woman) 'I've left (and I'm on my way)'. The same pattern gives **अडकलोय / अडकलेय** 'I'm stuck', **पोहोचलोय** 'I've arrived', and for others **तो निघालाय**, **ती अडकलेय**.

**About to:** **-णार आहे** 'going to', and with **-च** 'just about to': **मी निघणारच आहे** 'I'm just about to leave'. In the past it means 'was just about to': **मी तुलाच फोन करणार होतो** 'I was just going to call you'.

**Be right there:** **आलोच!** (man) / **आलेच!** (woman) — literally 'I've just come', used for 'I'm coming this second'. Similarly **पोहोचतोच** 'I'm just about there'.

**On the way:** **मी रस्त्यात आहे** or **वाटेत आहे**. **In X minutes:** **पाच मिनिटांत** (-आंत 'within').

The trap: these forms change for the speaker's gender — a woman says **निघालेय, अडकलेय, आलेच**.

examples.native: मी आत्ता निघालेय, वीस मिनिटांत पोहोचते.
examples.roman: mī āttā nighāley, vīs miniṭānt pohotste.
examples.en: I've just left, I'll be there in twenty minutes. (woman)
I was just about to call you! (woman)

dialogue.title: Saturday film plan
dialogue.setting: Pune. Friday evening, Neha calls her friend Aditya about the weekend. Then Saturday, 6:10 pm, outside a mall in Viman Nagar.

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: अरे आदित्य, उद्या संध्याकाळी फ्री आहेस का?
lines.roman: are āditya, udyā sandhyākāḷī frī āhes kā?
lines.en: Hey Aditya, are you free tomorrow evening?

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.native: हो, काही खास नाही. का? काय बेत आहे?
lines.roman: ho, kāhī khās nāhī. kā? kāy bet āhe?
lines.en: Yeah, nothing special. Why? What's the plan?

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: नवीन मराठी पिक्चर आलाय. चल, बघूया!
lines.roman: navīn marāṭhī pikchar ālāy. tsal, baghūyā!
lines.en: There's a new Marathi film out. Come on, let's see it!

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.en: Awesome! Where? The mall in Viman Nagar?

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: हो. शो साडेसहाचा आहे. सहा वाजता गेटवर भेटूया.
lines.roman: ho. sho sāḍesahātsā āhe. sahā vādztā geṭvar bheṭūyā.
lines.en: Yes. The show's at six thirty. Let's meet at the gate at six.

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.en: Done. And tea at the stall first?

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: चालेल! पण उशीर करू नकोस हं!
lines.roman: tsālel! paṇ ushīr karū nakos haṃ!
lines.en: Sure! But don't be late, OK!

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: अरे, कुठे आहेस? मी केव्हापासून थांबलेय!
lines.roman: are, kuṭhe āhes? mī kevhāpāsūn thāmbley!
lines.en: Hey, where are you? I've been waiting for ages!

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.native: सॉरी सॉरी! मी निघालोय, पण नगर रोडला ट्रॅफिकमध्ये अडकलोय.
lines.roman: sorī sorī! mī nighāloy, paṇ nagar roḍlā ṭræfikmadhye aḍakloy.
lines.en: Sorry, sorry! I've left, but I'm stuck in traffic on Nagar Road.

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.en: Same as always! How long will you be?

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.native: दहा मिनिटं. तू तिकिटं काढ, मी तुला पैसे देतो.
lines.roman: dahā miniṭaṃ. tū tikiṭaṃ kāḍh, mī tulā paise deto.
lines.en: Ten minutes. You get the tickets, I'll pay you back.

lines.speaker: Neha
lines.native: ठीक आहे. पण पिक्चर सुरू झाला तर पॉपकॉर्न तुझ्याकडून!
lines.roman: ṭhīk āhe. paṇ pikchar surū dzhālā tar pôpkôrn tujhyākaḍūn!
lines.en: OK. But if the film's started, the popcorn's on you!

culture: Plans among friends in Pune and Mumbai are made late and loosely, usually in a WhatsApp group: 'tonight?' at five o'clock is normal. Every Pune neighbourhood and college has its **कट्टा**, the ledge, steps or corner where the same group gathers in the evening, and the **टपरी** round the corner supplies cutting chai. Time is stretchy: **मी निघालोय** and **आलोच!** are often said by someone still at home, and Puneris joke about it endlessly — but offices, trains and anything with a ticket are another matter. A flat **नाही** to an invitation sounds harsh, so people soften it: **आज नाही जमणार**, **बघू** 'we'll see', **परत कधीतरी** — and बघू very often means no. With friends you use **तू** and the bare commands (ये, चल, थांब), but if a friend's parent answers the phone or the door, switch at once to **तुम्ही**, **अहो** and **काका / काकू**, and to **या, बसा**.

lessons.title: Asking if a friend is free

tip.title: तुला जमेल का? — can you make it?
tip.body:
- **जमणे** 'to work out for someone' takes **-ला**, like आवडणे: **तुला** जमेल का? 'can you make it?', **मला** नाही जमणार 'I can't make it'.
- Ask a friend **फ्री आहेस का?**; someone you call तुम्ही **फ्री आहात का?**
- **बेत** and **प्लॅन** both mean 'plan': आज काय बेत आहे?

sentences.native: मला शनिवारी जमणार नाही, मी बिझी आहे.
sentences.roman: malā shanivārī dzamṇār nāhī, mī bizī āhe.
sentences.en: I can't do Saturday, I'm busy.

sentences.roman: mī ādz khūp bizī āhe, udyā bolū.
sentences.en: I'm really busy today, let's talk tomorrow.

tip.title: Let's: -ऊया · Shall we?: -आयचं का?
tip.body:
- **Let's** = stem + **ऊया**: कर → **करूया**, जा → **जाऊया**, भेट → **भेटूया**, खा → **खाऊया**.
- Put **चल** (one friend) or **चला** (a group) in front: चल, जाऊया.
- **Shall we?** = **-आयचं का?**: जायचं का? काय करायचं?
- Not जाणार आहोत — that's 'we are going to', a plan, not a suggestion.

sentences.en: Come on, let's go to a film today.
Shall we meet at the mall?
Let's sit in a café and chat.
What shall we do tonight?
Shall we all go out to eat together?
It'll be loads of fun!

sentences.native: घरी बसून कंटाळा आलाय, काहीतरी करूया!
sentences.roman: gharī basūn kaṇṭāḷā ālāy, kāhītarī karūyā!
sentences.en: I'm bored sitting at home, let's do something!
Shall we eat something after the film?
You guys are going? I'm coming too!
Shall we go and hang around the mall?

tip.title: Commands between friends: ये, थांब, सांग
tip.body:
- To a friend (तू): the bare stem — **ये, थांब, सांग, चल**. To a group or politely: **या, थांबा, सांगा, चला**.
- Soften with **ना** (ये ना 'do come'), **रे / गं**, or push with **की** (सांग की! 'just tell me!').
- 'Don't': **करू नकोस** (तू), **करू नका** (तुम्ही).
tip.pattern: ये / या · ये ना · करू नकोस

tip.title: निघालोय · निघणारच आहे · आलोच!
tip.body:
- **I've left:** निघालो आहे → **निघालोय** (man) / **निघालेय** (woman); same for **अडकलोय** 'I'm stuck'.
- **Just about to:** **-णारच आहे**: मी निघणारच आहे. 'Was about to': **-णार होतो**.
- **आलोच! / आलेच!** = 'be right there!'
- Watch the speaker's gender: a woman says **निघालेय, अडकलेय, आलेच**.

sentences.en: I'm just about to leave, see you in ten minutes.

tip.title: Saying no softly
tip.body:
- **आज नाही जमणार** 'I can't make it today' is the friendly no; add **सॉरी यार**.
- Keep the door open: **पुढे ढकलूया?** 'shall we postpone?', **परत कधीतरी?** 'some other time?'.
- **बघू** 'we'll see' often means no.
- English **कॅन्सल** takes **करणे** (I cancel it) or **होणे** (it gets called off).

sentences.native: सॉरी, आज मला नाही जमणार, ऑफिसमध्ये खूप काम आहे.
sentences.roman: sorī, ādz malā nāhī dzamṇār, ôfismadhye khūp kām āhe.
sentences.en: Sorry, I can't make it today, there's loads of work at the office.

sentences.roman: pāūs āhe, tyāmuḷe plæn kænsal dzhālā.
sentences.en: It's raining, so the plan's off.

sentences.native: मी प्लॅन कॅन्सल केला नाही, फक्त पुढे ढकलला.

sentences.native: सॉरी यार, आज खरंच नाही जमणार, उद्या नक्की.
